speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have yellowing of the skin and eyes, which suggests jaundice. Can you tell me if you have experienced any abdominal pain, nausea, or changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, have you noticed any dark, tea-colored urine or pale, clay-colored stools? I also need to know if you have experienced any right upper quadrant abdominal pain or fever.

text: Your liver function tests indicate severe acute liver failure, but the viral hepatitis panel is negative. Given your history of drug use, have you taken any acetaminophen or other medications recently, and did you consume alcohol heavily in the days leading up to these symptoms?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of liver disease or iron overload, and have you consumed any energy drinks or herbal supplements recently? I need to rule out Wilson's disease or toxic hepatitis from other sources.

text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

text: Given your age, severe liver failure with a low alkaline phosphatase-to-bilirubin ratio, and psychiatric agitation, I strongly suspect Wilson's disease. REQUEST TEST: Ceruloplasmin, Urine_Copper, Slit_Lamp_Examination
